title: Seasonal Phytoplankton Responses to Environmental Variables in Lagos Lagoon, Nigeria (West Africa)
content:
ABSTRACT

An ecosystem's ability to interact with biotic and abiotic factors typically reveals its health and functionality. Twelve sites in Lagos Lagoon were sampled monthly over an entire year, covering the wet and dry seasons on the water parameters and phytoplankton composition to determine their seasonal link. A two-way factorial ANOVA (p < 0.05) revealed significant seasonal differences in water temperature, pH, EC, turbidity, salinity, DO, phosphate, and zinc. A total of 40 phytoplankton species were recorded from the study area. Four major algal groups were in the order of: Bacillariophyta > Cyanophytoa > Dinophyta > Clorophyta concerning their quantitative abundance. Notable species were Aulacoseira sp., Coscinodiscus sp., Bacillaria sp., Biddulphia sp., Hemisdiscus sp., Chaetoceros sp., Ceratium sp., Thalassionema sp., Oscillatoria sp., and Microcystis sp. across the wet and dry seasons of the study. Turbidity, EC, salinity, DO, TDS, nitrate, and COD showed a strong affinity with the distribution of phytoplankton community as evident from canonical correspondence analysis. The Margalef and Shannon-Wiener diversity indexes indicated moderately rich phytoplankton diversity in the lagoon ecosystem. The findings provide relevant information on the seasonal phytoplankton response to water parameters in Lagos Lagoon.
